memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the servant left, taking with him ten of his master's camels loaded with all kinds of good things from his master. He set out for Aram Naharaim and made his way to the town of Nahor. He had the camels kneel down near the well outside the town; it was toward evening, the time the women go out to draw water. Then he prayed, 'LORD, God of my master Abraham, make me successful today, and show kindness to my master Abraham. See, I am standing beside this spring, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water. May it be that when I say to a young woman, "Please let down your jar that I may have a drink," and she says, "Drink, and I'll water your camels too"—let her be the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown kindness to my master.'" - Gen 24:10-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Far from home, with a heavy responsibility, the servant does the wisest thing possible — he prays. And notice how he prays. He does not ask for a beautiful or wealthy girl. He asks for a sign of character: a young woman generous enough to water a stranger and even his ten thirsty camels. Watering camels was hard, tiring work. He was quietly praying for kindness, humility, and a servant's heart.

This is prayer that fits God's own heart. The servant lines up his request with the kind of person God delights in, rather than with outward appearances. He also prays specifically, honestly, and with dependence — "make me successful today."

We can learn to pray like this. When you seek God's guidance, ask Him to show you character, not just convenience. Bring your real needs plainly before Him. And remember, the servant's confidence was not in his clever plan but in God's kindness to his master.

Above all, notice that he prays before he acts. So often we act first and pray only when we are stuck. Begin at the well of prayer, and let God lead from there.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I pray before I act, or only when I am stuck?
2. Am I seeking character or only convenience in my choices?
3. How specific and honest are my prayers?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to pray before I act, and to seek the things You value. Lead me clearly and kindly, for I depend on You. Amen.
